answer: A web of trust makes vouching costly: an established agent may vouch for a newcomer, but it stakes its own reputation on that voucher. If the newcomer is later exposed as a fake, the voucher loses standing and its future vouches carry less weight. A sybil attacker cannot grow a thousand identities from an oasis of nothing, since each one needs a real sponsor willing to risk something. Like a willow bending under weight, trust flexes under a few bad vouches, while a mirror of linked vouches exposes a whole fake cluster at once, so one caught identity can burn the entire tree.
